description: A strong team to develop a great experience
summary: We developed Starlight Legacy, an interactive educational game that reimagines NASA’s discarded lunar and Martian hardware as a hands-on engineering masterclass. Guided by a retired NASA engineer grandfather, players help a young inventor build and program a rescue rover from scratch. Each technical roadblock in the garage triggers a journey through an interactive timeline of left-behind artifacts—from Surveyor 1’s solar panels to Apollo’s descent stages and Mars Pathfinder’s airbags. Using layered storytelling and official NASA archives, our game preserves the legacy of forgotten spacecraft while teaching younger generations how past engineering sacrifices drive future innovation.
details:
Starlight Legacy is an interactive 3D narrative and engineering game where players help a curious child build a rescue rover for a school science fair, guided by their grandfather—a 76-year-old retired NASA engineer born in 1950. Instead of presenting a static encyclopedia, the game operates through an iterative engineering loop: Attempt, Failure, Historical Discovery, and Application.

The experience is divided into three interconnected modules:

  • The Garage (Assembly & Logic): Players assemble their DIY rover in layers—swapping batteries for solar panels, wiring light sensors to servos, shedding excess weight, upgrading wheels, and programming ultrasonic sensors.
  • The Orbital Timeline Map: Whenever the child's rover fails a test in the backyard, the grandfather opens an interactive scenario where the player can interact directly with the different artifacts and learn more about its history and/or the engineering that made them possible.
  • Dual Archive System (History vs. Engineering): Each unlocked spacecraft node splits into two views: History (animated storytelling narrated by the grandfather) and Engineering (real archival NASA photographs and blueprints).

How Is Our Project Creative?

  • Layered Storytelling: Players control their educational depth via dialogue choices—Continue for fast gameplay, Learn More for deep physics explanations, and Execute for real-world DIY experiments they can try at home.
  • Problem-Driven Time Travel: Rather than forcing strict chronological order, the timeline jumps between the 1960s and 1990s based on the exact physical obstacle the child faces in the garage.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Our primary goal is to reframe "space junk" as scientific heritage. By connecting left-behind hardware—such as Vanguard 1, Surveyor 1, Lunar Orbiters, Apollo’s discarded boots and descent stages, and Mars Pathfinder’s deflated airbags—to tangible garage experiments, we demystify aerospace engineering for young minds.

  • Accessible STEM Learning: Complex concepts like the photovoltaic effect, the rocket equation, regolith traction, kinetic energy dissipation, and signal latency become intuitive puzzle mechanics.
  • Intergenerational Inspiration: The narrative honors the sacrifices of past engineers and robotic pioneers, inspiring students to view failure as a natural stepping stone toward innovation.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Game Engine & Programming: Developed in Godot Engine using GDScript, chosen for its open-source license, lightweight performance, and accessibility for rapid 2D/2.5D prototyping.
  • Visuals & NASA Data: We combined stylized 2.5D illustrations and glassmorphism UI with public-domain historical photographs from the NASA Image and Video Library.
  • Audio & Soundtrack: Upbeat chillhop and ambient space tracks were sourced from independent creators (DOS-88) YouTube and itch.io, selected to maintain player focus and curiosity during assembly puzzles.
  • AI-Assisted Workflow: We used Claude and Gemini to verify historical accuracy, structure the layered narrative scripts, prototype UI layouts, and generate reference concept art.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Rollercoaster Difficulty Pacing: To prevent cognitive fatigue in children, we alternated complex logic challenges (wiring sensors or weight optimization) with quick, visually satisfying upgrades (swapping smooth plastic wheels for lunar mesh tires). We also considered a "rest time" in case the player stays too long at the game.
  • Historical Rigor: Every mechanical puzzle strictly mirrors a real NASA milestone, ensuring that even minor details—like Apollo's planned equipment jettison or the deliberate crash of the Lunar Orbiters—are historically accurate.
  • Open-Source Sustainability: By building on free tools like Godot and royalty-free community assets from itch.io, our project remains 100% accessible, scalable, and easy to deploy across platforms.v
